content_voiceover: This is the MORPHO trial of gilteritinib maintenance after allogeneic transplant in FLT3 dash ITD positive AML, and it's an important contrast to the sorafenib data. The primary endpoint, relapse free survival in the overall population, was not statistically significant, hazard ratio zero point six seven nine, P equals zero point zero five one eight, just missing significance. Overall survival was similar between arms. However, in a pre-specified subgroup analysis using a sensitive FLT3 ITD measurable residual disease assay with a threshold of ten to the negative sixth, gilteritinib clearly improved relapse free survival in MRD positive patients, hazard ratio zero point five one five, while there was no benefit in MRD negative patients. The note in red reminds us this is not an FDA approved indication and is not reimbursed by Taiwan's National Health Insurance, so it's important for exam purposes to distinguish gilteritinib maintenance, which failed its primary endpoint, from sorafenib maintenance, which succeeded.
keypoints: MORPHO trial: gilteritinib maintenance after allo-HSCT missed primary RFS endpoint
Overall population HR zero point six seven nine, P equals zero point zero five, not significant
MRD positive subgroup benefited: HR zero point five one five
Not FDA approved for this indication, not reimbursed
keypoint_voiceover: MORPHO's gilteritinib maintenance missed its primary relapse free survival endpoint overall, but a pre-specified MRD positive subgroup, using a very sensitive ten to the minus six assay, did benefit. It's not an approved indication, so distinguish this from the positive sorafenib SORMAIN result.
